categories.title: Getting started
categories.hint: Connect your interface, create a project and learn the window.

topics.title: Record, mix and export
topics.keywords: start begin tutorial first time how to use
topics.intro: The whole path, from the first recording to the final file.
steps: Connect your audio interface and choose it in **Settings → Inputs and outputs**.
In **Projects**, click **New project** and choose **Video + audio** or **Audio only**.
Create a track with the **+** at the foot of the track headers and arm it with its **●**.
Record with {key:record}. Press it again to stop and save the channel.
Go to the **Mixer** with {key:mixer} and set volume, pan and effects.
Click {icon:E896} **Export MP4** or **Export audio**, at the top right.

topics.title: Connect your audio interface
topics.keywords: sound card driver asio input output headphones speakers setup
topics.intro: XTreme records and plays through ASIO, your interface's driver.
steps: Install the maker's ASIO driver and connect the interface before opening the app.
Under **Interface**, choose your driver.
Under **Channels**, choose **Stereo**, **Mono 1** or **Mono 2**, depending on where your guitar or mic is plugged in.
Under **Output**, choose the interface's output: it has the lowest latency.
Play your guitar and check that the input meter moves, at the bottom next to the transport.
notes: If audio drops out, raise the **Buffer** from **Driver panel**. If playing feels slow, lower it.

topics.title: Create or open a project
topics.keywords: new manager projects template open folder file xtp start song
topics.intro: Each song is a project with its own folder. The app starts in **Projects** or in an empty project.
steps: Click **New project** and give it a name.
Choose **Video + audio** or **Audio only**.
Choose a template, or start without tracks. Templates bring tracks, effects and the Reverb and Delay buses.
To open an existing one, click it in the list or use **Open…** and choose its **.xtp** file, wherever it is.
To save it in another folder, click **Save in…** before creating it.
notes: The list shows every project you made or opened, wherever it is, with its folder under the name.
To return to the list from an open project, click the project name in the top bar or open **File → Projects…**.
To start straight in an empty project, turn off **Show at startup** at the bottom of **Projects**, or choose **Empty project** in Settings → Saving and export. **Save** asks where it goes.

topics.title: Choose video or audio only
topics.keywords: mode no camera music mp3 wav
topics.intro: The switch at the top left sets the kind of project.
steps: **Video + audio**: camera, one panel per track and MP4 export.
**Audio only**: no camera or video, more room for the timeline. Exports WAV or MP3.
notes: You can switch at any time. Going back to video deletes nothing.

topics.title: Learn the window
topics.keywords: interface parts panels inspector timeline transport where is maximize enlarge enter
topics.intro: What each area holds.
steps: **Top**: project mode, name, save, undo, tools and **Export**.

**Left**: the selected track's inspector: its name, the track's settings, the selected clip's and, at the bottom, its strip: pan, M and S, the fader, the effects, the sends and the output. The buttons on top show or hide the clip and the strip; the edge between them sets the strip's height. {key:leftPanel} folds it.
**Center**: the video preview and the live camera.
**Below the preview**: the timeline, with tracks and clips. {key:mixer} swaps it for the mixer.
**Right**: project-wide things: Color, Patterns, Library and History. {key:rightPanel} folds it.

**Bottom**: clock, play, record, tempo, click, tuner and the Timeline, Piano roll, Mixer and Mastering views. Pressing the active view again goes back to the timeline. Without video the timeline is always on screen and its button is hidden.
**Maximize**: {key:maximize} or {icon:E740} gives the whole window to the panel you touched last (video, timeline, piano roll, mixer or mastering). Again, and everything goes back as it was.

topics.title: See what's new
topics.keywords: changes version new update release notes changelog
topics.intro: What changed in each version. It shows by itself the first time you open a new version.
steps: Open **Help → What's new**, click {icon:E789} in **Projects** or **What's new** in this help.
At the top, choose the version.
**See in help** opens that item's topic.

categories.title: Record
categories.hint: Recording, click, inputs, tuner, camera and latency.

topics.title: Record a channel
topics.keywords: recording rec guitar vocal microphone arm track
topics.intro: Recording goes to the armed tracks, from the playhead.
steps: Create a track with the **+** at the foot of the track headers, a right click on the empty part of the timeline, or {key:newTrack}.
Arm it with its **●** or with {key:arm}. It turns red.
Put the playhead where you want to start. {key:toStart} goes back to the beginning.
Record with {key:record}.
Stop with {key:record} or {key:play}. The channel stays on the track. With **Discard** and a second click to confirm, it doesn't.
notes: If **Record** is off, no track is armed.
Recordings are written to disk as you record. If the power fails, the recording is recovered when you open the project.

topics.title: Record several tracks at once
topics.keywords: multitrack simultaneous band drums several inputs
topics.intro: Each armed track records its own input, from the same instant.
steps: Arm all the tracks with their **●**.
Click each track's input chip and choose its input.
Record with {key:record}. You get one channel per track.

topics.title: Choose the input and hear yourself
topics.keywords: input monitoring monitor cant hear myself gain level clipping red
topics.intro: Each track chooses which input of the interface it records.
steps: Arm the track. A chip with its input appears.
Click the chip and choose the input or pair.
Set the gain on the interface so the meter stays out of the red.
To hear yourself, use the interface's direct monitoring. If it has none, turn on **Monitor** in the transport.
notes: **Monitor** adds latency: use it only if the interface has no direct monitoring.

topics.title: Use the click and count-in
topics.keywords: metronome bpm tempo count in tap bar
topics.intro: It's all in the transport box.
steps: Turn the click on with {key:click}.
Turn the count-in on with {key:countIn}: four beats before recording.
Type the tempo in **Tempo**, or tap it with {key:tap}.
The **▾** next to it chooses the click sound.
notes: The click never goes into recordings or exports.

topics.title: Re-record a section
topics.keywords: overdub redo fix mistake punch replace channel take
topics.intro: What you record again replaces only the section it covers.
steps: Put the playhead a little before the mistake.
Arm the track and record with {key:record}.
Stop after the section. What came before and after stays as it was.
notes: What was replaced isn't lost: it stays in **History** and **Library**.
**Lock clip** protects a good channel: recording won't overwrite it.

topics.title: Tune up
topics.keywords: tuner strings note guitar bass out of tune
topics.intro: It listens to the first armed track, or to input 1-2.
steps: Open the tuner with {key:tuner}.
Play one string alone.
Follow the blinking triangle to know whether to go up or down. Green means in tune.
notes: If it doesn't react, move **Sensitivity** in the same panel.

topics.title: Calibrate latency
topics.keywords: out of sync late early delay channel shifted calibration loopback
topics.intro: Makes what you record land exactly in time with what you were hearing.
steps: **With a cable**: connect an interface output to an input. Lower your headphones and measure. It's the most accurate.
**Playing**: without a cable, play a short note on each click.
Done: every new channel is compensated automatically.
notes: Calibrate again if you change interface or buffer. Each input and output pair keeps its own measurement.
To adjust a single channel, use **Audio offset** in the channel's **Sync** section.

topics.title: Record with a camera
topics.keywords: webcam phone droidcam video film ip
topics.intro: In a **Video + audio** project, the camera records along with the audio.
steps: Choose the camera and resolution in Settings. For a phone, **IP DroidCam**.
Check the picture in the live monitor, next to the preview.
Arm a video track and record with {key:record}. The video goes to the first armed track that carries video.

categories.title: Edit
categories.hint: Cut, move, copy, import, tempo, markers and undo.

topics.title: Move and trim clips
topics.keywords: clip drag shorten fade in out edges stretch
topics.intro: A clip is a piece of a recorded channel. Trimming doesn't touch the file.
steps: To **move** it, drag the clip, onto another track too. Drop it under the last track and it goes to a **new track** of the same kind (a MIDI one, with the same instrument).
To **trim** it, drag the lower handle on an edge.
To **stretch** it without changing the pitch, hold **Ctrl** and drag that handle. The label shows the speed against the recording. The clip goes quiet until its sound is ready.
To **fade**, drag the upper handle on an edge.

With the snap on, the clip's start lands on a grid line: **Auto** uses the nearest visible one and changes with the zoom; the fixed values go from **Bar** to **1/64**, with triplets (**T**) and dotted values (**D**), which start over at each bar. The ruler (right click) offers the same values for drawing the grid. To move it freely, hold **Alt** while dragging.
To **copy** it, hold **Shift** and drag the clip: the original stays where it was.
notes: **Restore trims and fades**, on right-click, puts it back.
Attacks stay in place when stretching: the stretch goes between them, so it works on rhythm loops.
**Snap to other clips**, next to the snap, sticks the start or end to another clip's edge.
{key:alignGrid}, or **Align to the grid** on right-click, lines up the picked clips.

topics.title: Split, duplicate, copy and paste
topics.keywords: cut scissors paste repeat join glue merge
topics.intro: Works on the selected clip or on all the marked ones.
steps: Put the playhead where you want to cut and split with {key:split}.
Duplicate with {key:duplicate}: the copy lands right after or, with the magnet on, on its next whole step.
Copy with {key:copy} or cut with {key:cut}.
Paste with {key:paste}: it starts at the playhead, on the selected track.
notes: On a MIDI clip, a note across the cut stays in both pieces and keeps sounding as one.
To join MIDI clips, mark them and use {key:joinClips} or right-click → Join clips: one clip per track is left, from the first to the last, sounding the same.
On a pattern, cut on the line between two passes to keep both pieces linked. Anywhere else, the right piece becomes a clip of its own.

topics.title: Loop a clip
topics.keywords: loop repeat extend passes garageband
topics.intro: Extends a clip by repeating it. Works on audio clips, MIDI clips and automation blocks.
steps: Hover the clip's top right corner: the two-arrow pointer appears.
Drag to the right: the clip repeats up to where you let go, and the last pass is cut there.
Each repeat shows the loop icon.
To change the original's length, drag the handle at the end of the first pass: every repeat follows.
To remove it, drag the corner back to the end of the first pass.
notes: On an audio clip, the repeats follow the original: move or trim it and they are made again. A repeat you edit by itself becomes a clip of its own.
On a MIDI clip, whatever you edit in any pass changes them all. On an automation block the passes show veiled and can't be edited: the original rules.

topics.title: Select several clips
topics.keywords: mark multiple selection rectangle group
topics.intro: To move, edit or delete several at once.
steps: Drag on the empty part of the tracks or of an automation lane: everything the rectangle touches is marked, automation blocks too.
**Ctrl+click** on a clip or a block adds or removes it.
**Shift+click** on a clip marks from the selected clip to that one, on the tracks between them.
Drag a marked block by its top strip and everything marked moves.
Drag one marked clip by its body and they all move; with Shift a copy of each stays where it was.
Drag an edge, a fade or the loop of a marked clip or block and they all change the same way.
Duplicate, copy, cut and paste take everything marked, blocks included: each block goes back to its own lane.
Delete them with {key:delete}.
{key:selectAll} marks every clip and block, and {key:deselect} clears the selection.

topics.title: Delete a section
topics.keywords: range remove part gap close
topics.intro: Takes a piece out of one or more tracks.
steps: Choose the **Range** tool ({key:toolRange}) and drag over the section. Dragging up or down adds tracks.
Delete with {key:delete}: the gap stays.
With {key:deleteClose}, what follows also shifts and closes the gap.
notes: Works on audio and MIDI clips.

topics.title: Use the tools
topics.keywords: scissors eraser hand magnifier zoom cursor select pencil brush draw paint
topics.intro: They're in the center of the top bar and change what a click does on the tracks.
steps: **Select** ({key:toolSelect}): the usual.
**Pencil** ({key:toolDraw}): click a clip to pick it and click an empty spot to place it; drag to position it.
**Brush** ({key:toolPaint}): like the pencil, but dragging repeats it along the stretch.
**Range** ({key:toolRange}): marks a section.
**Split** ({key:toolSplit}): one click cuts the clip.

**Erase** ({key:toolErase}): removes what it touches. With any tool, right-click and drag removes what it touches: clips, automation blocks, tempo points, meter changes, markers, chords and the loop range. A right-click without dragging opens the menu.
**Listen** ({key:toolListen}): hold down on a clip to hear that track alone.
**Zoom** ({key:toolZoom}) and **Hand** ({key:toolHand}): zoom in and move the view.
notes: A click on a pattern in Patterns or on a sample in the Library also picks it for the pencil and the brush.

They all work on the automation lanes too: Split cuts the block, Erase removes it, Listen plays its track, Range marks a stretch of its track (and deleting a range cuts its lanes too), and the pencil and the brush take a block with a click and lay copies on an empty spot (with no block taken, the click makes one).

topics.title: Move around the timeline
topics.keywords: zoom wheel scroll fit all track height grid snap
topics.intro: The wheel does nearly everything.
steps: **Wheel**: up and down.
{wheel:wheelZoom}: zoom in and out.
{wheel:wheelSideways}: sideways.
{wheel:wheelHeight}: track height.
{key:fit}: see the whole song.
notes: Right-click the ruler numbers to choose how the grid is drawn.
**Return on stop**, in the transport next to the loop: when on, stopping with {key:play} takes the playhead back to where playback started; while it plays, a dashed line marks that point.

topics.title: Import audio and use samples
topics.keywords: bring file wav mp3 sample loop drag library backing track copy link duplicate media mono stereo channels left right wave
topics.intro: What you import is copied into the project or linked where it is, without duplicating it.
steps: Drag the file onto the timeline, or click **New track → Import audio…**.
For your sound folders, open **Library → Samples** and add a folder.

Above the list, **All**, **Audio**, **Video**, **MIDI** and **Favorites** show only that type, without folders, and work together with the search. A **.mid** isn't auditioned: bringing it in puts it on the selected MIDI track or on new MIDI tracks, like **Import .mid…**.
Listen with the play button or with **Auto** on (it plays when picked), and drag the sample onto a track, from the list or from the player: its name, or the wave pulled up or down.
To bring several, pick them with **Ctrl** or **Shift** and drag them together: they land one under the other, on new tracks when there are no free ones.
Choose **Copy to project** or **Link**. **Don't show again** keeps that choice; change it in **Settings → Save and export**.
notes: A sample from the Library also drops into a plugin's window (a sampler, a drum machine), as from the Explorer.
If you move or delete a linked file, its clips go offline. In the Library they show the **Linked** mark.
To bring a linked file inside, click **Copy to project** on its row in the Library. Your file stays where it is.
If a file moved, click **Choose the file…** or **Search a folder…** in the Library or in the grey clip's menu.
Removing a linked channel from the Library (or with **Unlink unused**) takes it out of the project without asking: your file isn't touched. A package carries a copy of linked files.

Next to the track's name, a badge says whether its clips are **Mono**, **Stereo** or **Mixed** (some of each). On a stereo or mixed track, **Show left and right** (in the track's menu or the inspector) shows each side's wave, left on top and right below. **L R**, at the foot of the tracks, turns it on or off on every stereo track at once.
Formats only FFmpeg reads can't be linked: they come in as WAV.
Formats: WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A and AIFF. Some need FFmpeg.

topics.title: Change the volume inside a clip
topics.keywords: gain curve points raise lower part
topics.intro: To fix a phrase without touching the fader.
steps: Select the clip. Its volume line appears.
Click the line to add a point and drag it.
Double-click a point to remove it.
For the whole clip, use **Clip gain** in the channel's **Clip** section.

topics.title: Name a clip
topics.keywords: name rename label title clip region midi pattern
topics.intro: An audio or MIDI clip can have a name of its own, shown at the clip's top left.
steps: Right-click the clip → **Rename…**.
Type the name and press **Enter**. **Esc** cancels.
To take the name away, leave it blank.
notes: On a pattern's clip, it renames the pattern in every use.
On a looped clip, the name is the original's and every repeat carries it.
A clip without a name of its own shows no text.

topics.title: Reverse a clip
topics.keywords: backwards reversed flip effect
topics.intro: The clip plays backwards, in the same place. The file doesn't change.
steps: Right-click an audio clip → **Reverse**. Works with several marked clips too.
A small arrow appears on the clip.
Repeat to turn it back to normal.
notes: It doesn't apply to clips with video.

topics.title: Change or detect the tempo
topics.keywords: bpm speed faster slower stretch
topics.intro: Changing the tempo can change the speed of the whole song, keeping the pitch.
steps: Type the value in **Tempo**, in the transport.
If there are clips, choose **Stretch** so they follow the tempo, or **Grid only** to leave the audio as it is. Stretched, each clip goes quiet for a moment until its sound is ready.
To find an audio's tempo, right-click the clip → **Detect tempo**.
Choose **Set the project to N BPM**. That moves the grid and stretches nothing.

topics.title: Tempo and meter changes
topics.keywords: tempo track ramp meter time signature 7/8 6/8 3/4 accelerando ritardando follow tempo
topics.intro: The tempo track changes the tempo and meter along the song.
steps: Show it with its button next to the tools. The meter row is on top and the tempo curve below. Drag its bottom edge to make it taller.
Double-click the curve (or click with the Pencil) to add a point. Drag it in time and tempo: Alt moves it freely, Shift changes tempo only.
Right-click a point: **Ramp to next**, **Type tempo…** or **Delete** (also Del).
Double-click or right-click the meter row, or the ruler numbers, to change the meter from that bar.
notes: The first point can't move in time or be deleted.
MIDI clips, markers, chords and tracks with **Follow tempo** keep their bar. Other audio tracks stay in seconds: turn on **Follow tempo** by right-clicking the track.
With tempo changes, the transport's **Tempo** box shows the tempo at the playhead; typing there changes the speed of the whole song.

topics.title: Use markers and the loop
topics.keywords: repeat section chorus a-b range chapters youtube chords strip
topics.intro: Above the ruler there are three strips: range, markers and chords.
steps: Add a marker at the playhead with {key:marker}, or double-click the markers strip.
Jump between markers with {key:prevMarker} and {key:nextMarker}.
Drag in the range strip to mark the A–B range. The loop turns on. Double-click that strip to clear it.
Toggle the loop with {key:loop}. {key:loopIn} and {key:loopOut} set A and B at the playhead.
With the loop on and no A–B range, it repeats from the start to where the last clip ends. With the loop off, playback goes on past the end until you stop it.
notes: To write a chord, double-click the chords strip and type its name. Double-click a chord to rename it. Drag it to move it, or drag an edge to make it longer or shorter; with several marked, they move together.
Right-click the markers strip → **Copy chapters for YouTube**.
Three buttons next to the tools show or hide the range, markers and chords strips.

topics.title: Organize your tracks
topics.keywords: folder color icon name rename separator group move duplicate copy track
topics.intro: So a big project stays easy to read.
steps: Double-click a track's name to rename it.
Click its badge to choose color and icon. In the inspector, the square next to the name changes the color; on a folder, the button next to it gives that color to its tracks.
Drag a track by its handle to move it.
**New track → Folder** groups tracks: drag them in by their handle. {key:folderGroup} puts the picked tracks, or those of the selected clips, in a new folder.
Right-click the track → **Duplicate track** ({key:duplicateTrack}) copies it below with everything; **Duplicate without content**, only its sound.

In the mixer, right-click the empty space → **New separator** puts one where you clicked; **Separator** in the header puts it after the selected channel. Double-click a separator to pick its color, or its name to rename it.
notes: A folder is a channel too: its effects, pan and fader work on its tracks' sum, and its **S** plays only its tracks.
**Ctrl+click** on headers picks several tracks: right-click, {key:delete} and {key:duplicateTrack} act on all of them.

topics.title: Lock a clip or track
topics.keywords: protect pin padlock dont move
topics.intro: Locked items don't move, trim or delete, and recording won't overwrite them.
steps: Right-click the clip → **Lock clip**, or the track → **Lock track**.
A padlock {icon:E72E} appears.
Repeat to unlock.
notes: Volume, fades and framing can still be changed.

topics.title: Freeze a track
topics.keywords: freeze render cpu dsp load plugin instrument bounce
topics.intro: Renders a track's instrument and effects so they stop using DSP. The track's plugins close.
steps: Click the snowflake {icon:E9CA} in the track header, or right-click the track (in the timeline or the mixer) → **Freeze**.
The snowflake stays lit and its clips show dimmed under the render's wave.
To change something, click the snowflake again, or right-click → **Unfreeze**.
notes: Fader, pan, mute, solo and sends stay live and can be automated.
While frozen, its clips, notes, effects, instrument and Transpose can't be edited.
The render is saved in the project's freeze folder.

topics.title: Undo and go back
topics.keywords: ctrl z redo mistake recover version history steps
topics.intro: There are three levels, from the most immediate to the widest.
steps: Undo with {key:undo} and redo with {key:redo}.
**History → Steps**: every change in this session. One click goes to that point.
**History → Versions**: saved copies of the project. Click **Save version** before trying something big.
**History → Exports**: go back to the exact mix of an exported file.
notes: Going back to a version saves the current state first, and what you recorded later isn't lost.

categories.title: Mix
categories.hint: Mixer, effects, reverb and delay, automation and A/B.

topics.title: Edit several tracks at once
topics.keywords: several tracks select multiple group together transpose volume pan mute all
topics.intro: With several tracks picked, the inspector changes what they have in common.
steps: On the timeline, **Ctrl+click** or **Shift+click** the track headers.
The inspector shows how many you picked and keeps only what they share: the fader, the pan, **Output**, the sends they all have and **Transpose**.
Move a control: every track gets the same value, and **Undo** brings them back together.
If a value differs between them, the control reads **Mixed** until you change it.
Locked tracks don't change: the note on top says how many stay out.

topics.title: Use the mixer
topics.keywords: console fader volume pan mute solo channels level
topics.intro: One strip per track, with the master fixed on the right.
steps: Open it with {key:mixer}.
Raise or lower each track with its fader. The pan bar moves it left or right.
**M** mutes ({key:mute}) and **S** soloes the track ({key:solo}).
Watch the master meter: the red light on top means the level went over.
notes: {wheel:wheelZoom} over the mixer changes the channel width, also over a knob or a fader: with that key held no value changes.

**Effects** and **Sends**, at the top, show or hide that section on every strip. Drag the line under a list to make it taller or shorter; a double click fits it to the longest list. Right-click the button: the same fit or the default height.

**Audio**, **MIDI**, **Folders**, **Buses**, **Separators** and **Empty**, in the header, show or hide each kind of strip. Without folders, their tracks stay in the folder's place. The mixer has two sides: the left one and the right dock, each scrolling on its own. Channels go on the left and buses in the right dock by default; right-click a strip → **Dock** moves it to **Dock left** or **Dock right**. Drag the line between the left side and the right dock to give one more room, and double-click it to reset. Drag a bus anywhere, between the channels too: it stays after the channel on its left.

**View**: the mixer's title is a drop-down (Mixer · XTreme) that changes its layout. **XTreme**: the free one, the only one with zoom; width, effects, sends and their heights, names and inspector are yours, and stay as you left them when you come back to it. The others are fixed, like FL Studio's: no zoom, and their own sections. **Compact** and **Wide**: strips keep pan, fader and meter, and the selected channel's effects, sends, input and output go in the inspector, at the side. **Compact alt** and **Wide alt**: the same, with names at the bottom. **Console**: every strip has its own effects and sends, no inspector.

**Inspector** shows the selected channel in a full-height panel: input, output, all its effects, sends and pan. Drag its edge to resize it. Right-click the panel: **Inspector on the left** or **on the right**.
The three dots over each fader share the height between the lists and the fader; double-click resets it.
Strip names can go at the bottom: Settings → Appearance → Mixer.
**MONO**, on the master, lets you check the mix in mono.
Right-click a strip: the same actions as on the track header.

topics.title: Add and reorder effects
topics.keywords: plugin vst compressor eq equalizer saturation gate chorus insert
topics.intro: Each channel has its effect list, which plays from top to bottom.
steps: Select the track.
Click the **+** of **Effects** on the inspector's strip, or the one on its mixer strip.
Pick the effect by category. Your VST plugins are at the end.
Click an effect in the list to open it in its window. Drag it to move it.
The **⋯** or right-click turns it off, duplicates or removes it.
notes: Built-in effects are grouped: **Dynamics**, **Classic compressors**, **EQ**, **Saturation**, **Modulation**, **Space and stereo** and **Mastering** (the mastering chain stages, in order).

Clicking a built-in effect opens its window, under where you clicked. Move it by its bar; it stays open while you work and you can have several. Close it with its X or **Esc**. It shows every control, in panels.

Each effect has its own identity: what matters goes on big knobs, its graph sits on top (the reverb's tail, the delay's echoes, the modulation's wave, the saturation's curve, the stereo field, the tone effects' response) and it takes its family's color: violet for dynamics, green for tone, orange for drive, blue for space and pink for modulation.

topics.title: Classic compressors
topics.keywords: compressor classic fet opto optical vca bus vari-mu tube 1176 la-2a ssl dbx fairchild glue
topics.intro: Five compressors with the character of the most used studio units, each with its own controls and way of reacting.
steps: Click **+ Effect** → **Classic compressors** and pick one.
**FET**: fast and aggressive, attack from 20 µs. Turn **Input** up for more compression (the level is compensated); **All** puts the four ratios in at once.
**Opto**: smooth and musical. Just **Reduction** and **Gain**; the cell sets attack and release by the program.
**Bus VCA**: clean, to glue a mix or a group. Stepped ratio, attack and release, **Auto**, and **SC HPF** so the lows don't pump it.
**Classic VCA**: reads the average (RMS) and releases at 120 dB/s; punchy on kicks and bass. **Hard** or **Soft** knee, ratio up to ∞.
**Vari-Mu**: tube, a ratio that grows with the level, and color. **Time** 1 to 4 fixed, 5 and 6 automatic.
notes: **Dry** and **Wet** give parallel compression.
The panel's graph shows the curve, with a dot where the signal is, and the last seconds of input, output and reduction. Every compressor has it, the **Compressor** in Dynamics too.
The strip's reduction meter shows how much each one compresses.
Every knob can be automated.

topics.title: Pump: tempo sidechain
topics.keywords: sidechain pump ducking kickstart kick bass pad volume tempo
topics.intro: **Pump** ducks the volume on every beat and lets it come back, like a compressor sidechained to the kick, with no routing.
steps: On the track (or bus) you want to breathe, click **+ Effect** → **Dynamics** → **Pump**.
On top, **Tempo** or **Sidechain**, and how often it ducks: 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 or 1/1.
The big knob, **Depth**, is how far it drops.
Under the graph, pick a **shape**; **Length** (how much of the beat it takes to come back) and **Curve** fine-tune it.
notes: It follows the project's tempo and lands on the beat wherever you start.
Beside them: **Attack** (how fast it drops) and **Offset** (ahead of or behind the beat).

The graph shows the curve over the sound (what comes in, dim; what goes out, in color) and a line that rides it with what is playing. With **Sidechain**, the bar on the right is the driving track's level: it fires when it crosses the accent line.

With **Sidechain** the other track shapes it: the louder it plays, the more it ducks (a soft hit ducks less, a long note holds it down) and it comes back along the **Curve**. The knobs become a compressor's: **Threshold** (Auto: 24 dB under its recent peak; 24 dB over the threshold it ducks all the way), **Attack**, **Hold** and **Release**.
The strip's reduction meter shows how far it drops.

topics.title: Tonal balance
topics.keywords: tonal balance spectrum mastering reference lows highs punch mid side genre dubstep riddim trap reggaeton metal house techno drum bass lofi
topics.intro: **Tonal balance** compares the mix's frequency balance with a target. It doesn't change the sound.
steps: On the master or on any track or bus, click **+ Effect** → **Analysis** → **Tonal balance**. On the master it always goes last, after **Output**: it reads what goes out, limiter included.
Choose the **target**: a genre, or **Reference…** to build it from one or more of your songs.
Play the mix: each band (**Lows**, **Low mids**, **High mids**, **Highs**) shows the target's range and where the mix is; when it falls outside, the mark changes color.
**Punch** is the low end's impact (crest factor under 120 Hz) against the target's range.
notes: Genres: Pop, Rock, Metal, Country / Folk, R&B / Soul, Hip-hop, Trap, Reggaeton / Urban, Reggae, Electronic (EDM), House / Techno, Dubstep, Riddim, Deep dubstep (UK), Drum & bass, Lo-fi, Acoustic / Jazz and Orchestral / Classical. The three dubstep targets differ in sub, mids and limiting: the menu says how on each.
The full view adds the mix's spectrum over the target's band.
**Stereo / Mid / Side**: both sides, only the center or only the sides.
**Response** is how long it averages (1 to 10 s). The reload button restarts the reading.
It compares shape, not level: turning the mix up or down doesn't change the reading.
The reference is saved in the project: the files are no longer needed.
It analyzes while its panel is on screen.

topics.title: Sidechain: let another track drive it
topics.keywords: sidechain kick bass ducking compressor gate pump ghost
topics.intro: A compressor, a gate or **Pump** can react to another track instead of their own: the bass ducks when the kick hits.
steps: On the track that should duck (the bass, the pad), add a **Compressor** or a **Pump**.
In the effect's **Sidechain** dropdown, pick the track that drives it (the kick).
Set the compressor's threshold and amount, or Pump's threshold, depth and release.
notes: It hears that track after its effects and before its fader: turning it down doesn't change how much it ducks the others.
A muted track still drives it: a "ghost" kick nobody hears works.
With a track picked, **Pump** ducks on each of that track's hits instead of on the beat.
A **Gate** with a sidechain opens when the other track plays.
If the driving track is removed, the effect goes back to its own signal.

topics.title: EQ with dynamic bands
topics.keywords: equalizer band dynamic de-esser sibilance harsh frequency graph large view
topics.intro: The **EQ** has 7 bands. A dynamic band acts only when that area goes over its level.
steps: Add an **EQ** to the track and choose a preset, or drag the points on the graph.
To make a band move by itself, select it and turn on **Dynamic**.
Set **Threshold** and **Range**. A negative range cuts; a positive one boosts.
**Large view** opens the same editor in a bigger window.
notes: Useful for an area that only bothers at certain moments, without cutting it through the whole song.

topics.title: Choose a compressor preset
topics.keywords: compressor preset vocal bass drums kick snare percussion piano synth strings winds bus mix voice-over podcast categories panels threshold ratio attack release
topics.intro: The compressor starts at **Default** and has presets by instrument and by use. They apply right away.
steps: Add a **Compressor** to the track.
Open the preset list and go through a category: **Vocals**, **Guitars**, **Bass**, **Drums**, **Percussion** and the rest.
Pick a preset and set **Amount**.
If it does not compress as expected, click **Analyze channel**, next to the preset: it fits threshold and level to it.
On a bus or the master use **Buses and mix**: they bind the sound without changing the level.
notes: **General** works on any sound.
The compressor's window shows every control in panels: **Dynamics**, **Timing**, **Output**, **Built-in EQ** and **Sidechain**.

topics.title: Effect presets: Default and your own
topics.keywords: preset presets default save my presets effect compressor eq reverb delay saturation gate template settings
topics.intro: Every built-in effect starts at **Default**: neutral, for any sound. From the preset list you pick another one or save your own.
steps: Open the effect and set it up.
Click **Save preset**, next to the list, and give it a name.
Your presets show in that effect's list, under **My presets**, in all your projects.
To delete one, pick it and click the trash can.
notes: With the same name, the preset is replaced.
Choosing **Default** takes the effect back to how it starts.
A preset doesn't change the effect's ON or its sidechain.

topics.title: Shape a guitar sound
topics.keywords: tone saturation drive compressor strumming arpeggio lead eq tube tape
topics.intro: A starting point with the built-in effects.
steps: **Saturation**: choose **Tube** (warm) or **Tape** (compact) and set the **Drive**.
**Compressor**: under **Guitars**, choose **Strumming**, **Arpeggio**, **Lead** or another preset, and set **Amount**.
**EQ**: choose a preset and fix what's left.
Use the **Gate** if there's noise or hum between notes.
notes: Project templates already bring these effects set up.

topics.title: Add reverb or delay
topics.keywords: echo ambience room bus send return fx
topics.intro: They go on a bus: a separate channel that several tracks send a little signal to.
steps: In the mixer, right-click → **New bus / FX channel**. Templates already bring Reverb and Delay.
On the bus, click **+** and add **Reverb** or **Delay**.
Select a track and click the **+** of **Sends** on the inspector's strip. Check the bus.
Raise the send level until it sounds right.
notes: **PRE** takes the send before the fader: it keeps sounding if you lower the track.
A bus sends to other buses too, with the same **+** under **Sends** in its strip. A bus that would send the sound back to it isn't offered; its output always goes to the Master.

**Connections**, in the mixer's header, shows the selected channel's active sends under the strips: a line to each bus, with a knob for its level. With a bus selected, the sends that reach it too, fainter. Ropes leave from OUT and arrive at IN, on either side of the selected strip; at the other end, under each knob, IN or OUT too, and the arrow comes up into it. Under each bus the channel doesn't send to yet, **Send** makes that send at once. Drag the band's top edge to make it taller. The channel's output (to its folder, a bus or the Master) is drawn apart: a thicker neutral line, without a knob. A selected bus or folder also shows what goes out to it.
When you stop, tails ring on until they fade. To silence them now, click **Cut audio** (the muted speaker in the transport) or press {key:cutAudio}: it also cuts notes left sounding.

topics.title: Automate volume and effects
topics.keywords: curve shape tension stairs pulse wave hold move by itself fade envelope parameter sampler cutoff resonance
topics.intro: Makes a control change by itself along the song.
steps: Right-click the control → **Automate…**, or the track's or folder's menu → **Automation**. In a plugin: click **Automate** in its window's bar and move the parameter.

A lane appears under the track, the folder's row or the bus's row. A bus with automation has its row at the end of the timeline (its lanes start from its strip's right click in the mixer); **Show buses in the timeline** (right click on a bus row or on the empty space) shows or hides them. A folder's lanes hide when it folds; **Show automation**, in its menu, shows or hides them.
Click adds a point, dragging moves it and double-click deletes it. Shift+drag draws. Right-drag erases the blocks it touches, as with clips.
Drag the circle in the middle of a segment to set its tension: bend it, or change how many stairs, pulses or waves it has. Double-click sets it back to zero.
Right-click a point or a segment → its shape: **Curve**, **Double curve**, **Hold**, **Stairs**, **Smooth stairs**, **Pulse** or **Wave**. A point's is the one of the segment coming into it.
Right-click a point → **Type value…**: type the value in the parameter's units (dB, Hz, ms, %, L/R) and press Enter.
Drag a block's top right corner to loop it. The passes show veiled and can't be edited: points go in the original.
To delete a lane, click the trash can in its header and confirm.
notes: With a lane on, moving that control by hand does nothing: the lane rules.
**Automate** turns off by itself once the lane is made; another click cancels it. A bus's effects don't have it.

topics.title: Compare two mixes
topics.keywords: a b ab before after mix versions
topics.intro: **A | B**, in the mixer bar, keeps two mixes of the same song. It comes hidden: show it in **Settings → Appearance → Mixer**.
steps: Make a mix in **A**.
Click **B**: it starts as a copy of A.
Change what you want and switch to compare.
notes: It doesn't touch tracks or the master. Right-click: **Copy A to B** and **Forget mix B**.

topics.title: Transpose a track
topics.keywords: pitch semitones up down tuning change key
topics.intro: Changes the pitch without changing the length.
steps: Select the track.

In the inspector, under **Transpose** (in the clip section), click or drag along the scale, use the wheel (Shift: an octave) or the arrow keys: −24 to +24 semitones. The top shows how far it is transposed and the interval ("Perfect 5th up"); double-click goes back to the original.
Wait for the notice: while it computes, the track sounds as before.
notes: To change **a single clip**: right-click the clip → **Pitch**. It goes from −12 to +12 and adds to the track's, up to ±24.

topics.title: Save a track's sound
topics.keywords: template preset reuse effect chain
topics.intro: A track preset keeps its effects, volume, color and input.
steps: Right-click the track → **Save as preset**.
To use it, **New track → Preset**.
To apply it to an existing track, right-click → **Use preset**.

categories.title: Master
categories.hint: Master chain, final loudness and limiter.

topics.title: Master in a few steps
topics.keywords: final loud finish polish chain limiter lufs
topics.intro: The last step before exporting. Open the **Mastering** view in the transport.
steps: Play the loudest part of the song.
At the top, choose the **Target** for where you'll publish.
Add effects with **+ Effect**, at the top (or **Full chain**). Click a tile in the chain to edit it below.
On the right, check that **True peak** stays under the **Ceiling** and watch the LUFS move in the graph.
notes: The power button next to **Master** turns the whole chain on or off, **Output** included (Soft clip and Limiter). Off, the mix passes untouched; the Target still sets the loudness.
Drag a tile by its grip to change the order. Right-click: its options.
Soft clip and Limiter always come last.

topics.title: Hit each platform's loudness
topics.keywords: lufs spotify youtube instagram tiktok apple music normalization quiet loud target limiter
topics.intro: Each platform normalizes to its own level. **Target** takes the mix there.
steps: In **Mastering**, top right, choose the **Target**: YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Spotify or Apple Music.
The app measures the mix and sets the gain by itself.
You hear and export at that loudness.
notes: With **As it is**, you set **Drive** by hand.
The **Limiter** keeps peaks under the **Ceiling**, −1 dB by default.

categories.title: Export
categories.hint: Audio, video, social media, stems and a single section.

topics.title: Export audio
topics.keywords: wav mp3 flac aiff ogg save bounce final mix file render advanced bits sample rate dither mono tail normalize
topics.intro: Renders the mix to a file.
steps: In an **Audio only** project, click **Export audio**, at the top right.
Choose **WAV** or **MP3**.
Click export. When it's done, a notice lets you open the file in Explorer.
notes: Files go to the project's **exports** folder. MP3 needs FFmpeg.

**Advanced**, below Quality, adds FLAC, AIFF and OGG, the bit depth (16, 24 or 32-bit float) with dither, the bitrate or VBR, the sample rate (44.1, 48 or 96 kHz), mono, a fixed tail in seconds, peak normalization (dBTP) and which tracks, folders or buses get a stem. Folded, it shows what you changed; left alone, the export is the same as always.
What you choose in Advanced is saved in the project for the next export.

topics.title: Export the video
topics.keywords: mp4 render upload reels shorts tiktok youtube instagram quality resolution 4k bitrate
topics.intro: What you see in the preview is what gets exported.
steps: Click **Export MP4**, at the top right.
Under **Destination**, choose **Project** or a platform: Reels, TikTok, YouTube, IG 1:1 or IG 4:5.
Choose the **Quality**.
Click export and wait. If there's a compatible graphics card, it's used.
notes: **Advanced** changes resolution (up to 4K) and bitrate.
Loudness isn't chosen here: it's the Mastering **Target**.

topics.title: Export only a section
topics.keywords: part fragment excerpt a-b
topics.intro: Exports what's between A and B, with the effect tails.
steps: Mark the A–B range in the ruler strip.
Open the export.
Under **Section**, choose **Loop A–B** instead of **Whole song**.

topics.title: Export each track separately
topics.keywords: stems separate tracks producer mixing engineer wav per track
topics.intro: To hand the song to someone else or to another program.
steps: Open the export.
Check the stems box.
Along with the file, you get a folder with one WAV per track.
notes: They all last the same, so they line up in any program.

topics.title: See if the song fits a platform
topics.keywords: duration length maximum story reel limit minutes
topics.intro: The timeline shows where each platform's limit falls.
steps: Right-click the ruler numbers.
Turn on the platforms you care about.
If the song runs over, the line turns amber and says **too long**.

categories.title: Video
categories.hint: Panels, format, framing, color and transitions.

topics.title: Set up the video panels
topics.keywords: split screen grid tracks in the video
topics.intro: Each video track is a panel.
steps: Choose the layout and format above the preview: **16:9**, **9:16** or **1:1**.
To take a track out of the picture, turn off **In the video** on its channel. It keeps sounding.
notes: For vertical video, try the **Vertical** layout from the layout button in the title bar.

topics.title: Frame a channel
topics.keywords: zoom move picture crop mirror panel
topics.intro: Framing belongs to each clip.
steps: In the preview, drag to move the picture.
Use the wheel to zoom.
The channel's **Framing** section has zoom, mirror and **Reset framing**.

topics.title: Correct the color
topics.keywords: filter look lut brightness contrast grain vignette cinema bars sharpness
topics.intro: The **Color** tab, in the right panel, applies to the whole video.
steps: Start with a **Filter**.
Refine it in **Adjustments**.
**Effects** has sharpness, vignette, grain and cinema bars.
Save what you like in **Templates**.

topics.title: Add a transition
topics.keywords: crossfade black cut join clips
topics.intro: Between two adjacent video clips, a square chip appears.
steps: Click the chip, at the join.
Choose **Cut**, **Crossfade** or **Dip to black**.
Choose the length. Sound fades along with the picture.
notes: It's also on the clip's right-click menu: **Transition in** and **Transition out**.

topics.title: Sync picture and sound
topics.keywords: out of sync lips late video early camera latency
topics.intro: If the picture arrives late compared to the audio.
steps: For what you record from now on, set **Camera latency** in Settings.
For a channel already recorded, use the channel's **Sync** section.

categories.title: MIDI and instruments
categories.hint: MIDI tracks, piano roll, VST, keyboards and patterns.

topics.title: Create a MIDI track and write notes
topics.keywords: piano roll notes drums beat compose draw
topics.intro: A MIDI track keeps notes and plays them with an instrument.
steps: **New track → MIDI track**. Or **MIDI track with instrument** and pick one: the track already plays with it. In the mixer, the same with a right click on the empty space.
Double-click an empty spot on the track: it creates a clip and opens the **Piano roll**.
Click on the grid to write a note. Drag to move it; its right edge lengthens it.
Right-click deletes.
Below, in **VEL**, you set how hard each note plays.
notes: {key:quantize} snaps the notes to the grid.
The piano roll has its own snap, or **Same as the timeline**.
What you play in the piano roll goes through the track's effects and fader: on a muted track you won't hear it.
What you play on a MIDI keyboard or the virtual keyboard lights up on the piano roll's keyboard and along its row.

topics.title: Scales and chords
topics.keywords: scale key root major minor pentatonic mode dorian chord triad inversion piano roll
topics.intro: Choose the song's scale and write chords with one click.
steps: In the **Piano roll**, or on the virtual keyboard, click **Scale** and choose the root and the scale.
The piano roll shows only the scale's rows, and notes you write or move land on it by themselves. A note already off the scale stays in sight, on its own row.
On the piano roll's bottom bar, turn on **Chords** ({key:chordTool}) and click a note: it writes the chord that belongs to it in the scale.

The selector appears over the chord: **R** is root position and **1**, **2** and **3** the inversions. Keys 1 to 4 work too, or {wheel:wheelHeight} over the chord (or over the one you are about to write). Each inversion stays close to where it was: the chord doesn't climb.
Drag the chord to move it: up and down it follows the scale, so it changes chord without leaving the key.
notes: **Alt** writes and moves outside the scale. A note out of the scale looks hollow.
The selector appears on any chord: select its notes with Ctrl+drag.
**Move notes to the scale**, in the scale picker, fixes what stayed out.

topics.title: Choose a VST instrument
topics.keywords: plugin sound piano synth kontakt sampler no sound test tone
topics.intro: Without an instrument, the track plays a test tone. Choose the **Sampler**, the **Granular**, a **General MIDI** instrument or a plugin.
steps: Select the MIDI track.
On the channel, open the **Instrument** dropdown, or right-click the track → **Instrument**.
Choose one from the list. The first time, installed plugins are scanned.
**Open its window** shows the plugin.

topics.title: General MIDI instruments
topics.keywords: volume search compact fold list next previous bank banks fluidr3 musescore download general midi gm soundfont sf2 piano drums bass strings program native instrument import mid song tracks channel 10 generaluser envelope attack release filter brightness resonance sensitivity velocity transpose tune mono glide
topics.intro: The 128 General MIDI instruments and the drum kits, with nothing to install.
steps: Under **Instrument**, open **General MIDI**: each family (Pianos, Guitars, Basses…) has its 8 instruments, and **Drums** has the kits.

**Open its window** (in the inspector or the piano roll) shows the instrument's window: on top, the one playing, ◀ ▶ for the previous or next one, the **Bank** and the instrument's **Volume**; below, the families and kits on the left, their instruments on the right (a click picks one), **Search instruments** and a keyboard to try it.
The list button, on top, folds the list away: the window shrinks and the instrument is picked from a menu by family.

In **Sound**, the knobs change the sound over the bank's, with the envelope and the filter drawn as they sound: **Envelope** (Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release), **Filter** (Brightness, Resonance, Vel. bright) and **Play** (Sensitivity, Transpose, Fine tune and, in **Mono**, Glide). At the centre it sounds as the bank does; a double click goes back there and **Reset** brings them all back.
When you import a **.mid** to new tracks, each track takes the instrument the file asks for; the one on channel 10 takes the drums, with each key named in the piano roll.
If the file has more than one track, **Import MIDI** asks which ones to bring. **All** and **None** tick or clear the list.
Each track takes the name it has in the file; without one, its instrument's.

**Bank**, at the top right of the window, picks the bank the track plays: **GeneralUser GS** (the lightest), **FluidR3 GM** or **MuseScore General** (more complete). Download them from there or in **Settings → Components** or **Load .sf2…** for one of your own.
notes: No bank comes with the app: until you download one, the track is silent and says so. Unless you pick another, it plays **GeneralUser GS**.
Each track keeps its bank. If it is missing on another PC, it plays another of the downloaded ones and the window says so.
Changing the instrument keeps the knobs as they were. Transpose doesn't apply to drums.
Importing onto a selected MIDI track puts the ticked tracks in a single clip. If that track plays the test tone, it takes the first one's instrument.

topics.title: Play a sample with the Sampler
topics.keywords: sampler sample wav loop one shot adsr envelope filter lfo drum instrument native root tune tuning detector note out of tune cents slide pan automate cutoff resonance
topics.intro: Play any sound across the keyboard.
steps: Drag an audio file onto a MIDI track. Or choose **Sampler** under **Instrument** and drop it in its window. The file stays linked where it is, without asking.
**Detected** shows the note the sound is on and how many cents it is off. **Tune** brings it to that note. You can also adjust it by hand with **Pitch** and **Fine**.
The **Root** is the key that plays it as it is. To change it, right-click a key.
Drag the **S** and **E** flags to choose which part plays.
Under **Mode**: **Note** sounds while the note lasts; **One shot** plays whole, for drum hits.
Choose a **Loop** so it keeps sounding while the note lasts, and move it with the **L** flags.
The loop's seam always blends (at least 5 ms; **Crossfade** makes it longer). **Snap to zero** puts the flags where the wave crosses zero, for an even cleaner blend. Alt leaves them free.
The wheel zooms the wave down to each sample. **Loop start** and **Loop end** go straight to each flag; a double-click shows it whole again.
Drag the envelope's points, and try the **Filter** and the **LFO**.
notes: Detection looks at the part between **S** and **E**. A drum hit has no clear pitch.
A note's slide, portamento and pan sound in the Sampler, note by note.
Right-click **Cutoff**, **Reso**, **Drive**, **Env**, **Volume**, **Pan** or what the LFO moves: **Automate…**.
The sample stays in the project, like any import.
One sample per track, for now.

topics.title: Stretch and texture with the Granular
topics.keywords: granular grains grain stretch time stretch scrub texture pad ambient density size jitter spray width position speed sync instrument native
topics.intro: Play a sample in short grains: stretch time without changing pitch, or freeze it at one point.
steps: Choose **Granular** under **Instrument** and drop an audio file in its window (it stays linked where it is). From the Library: right-click → **Open in the granular**.
Drag the **S** and **E** flags to choose the part the playhead goes over.
Under **Playhead**: **Stretch** runs through the sample at its **Speed** (100% is the original; slower makes it longer without lowering the pitch). **Scrub** keeps the playhead at the **Position**.
**Sync** makes the speed follow the project's tempo: set the sample's tempo in **BPM**.
Under **Grain**: **Density** is grains per second (or a note value, with **Sync**), **Size** how long each one lasts, and **Shape** and **Skew** its envelope.
**Jitter** loosens the grains' rhythm, **Spray** moves them away from the playhead and **Width** spreads them across the stereo field.
Each note plays at its pitch from the **Root**; right-click a key to change it.
notes: Right-click **Position**, **Speed**, **Density**, **Size**, **Jitter**, **Spray**, **Width**, **Volume** or **Pan**: **Automate…**. A lane on **Position** in **Scrub** moves the playhead through the sample.
With the position still and no Jitter or Spray, the grains repeat evenly and the sound buzzes at the density: raise Jitter or Spray a little to smooth it.
The sample stays in the project, like any import.

topics.title: Install and manage plugins
topics.keywords: vst vst2 vst3 32 bits folder scan not showing hide thumbnail picture category maker vendor group sort list
topics.intro: XTreme uses VST3 and VST2 plugins, 64 and 32 bits, each in its own process: if one crashes, recording goes on.
steps: Install the plugin as usual.
Click **Scan for new**.
If it's in another folder, add it with **+**.
Uncheck the ones you don't want in the menus.

In **Show in menus** pick **By maker**, **By category** or **List**; also from any plugin menu, in its **Show in menus** entry (a right click leaves the menu open). Each plugin's chip changes its category or makes a new one; **Automatic** goes back to the one the app detects.
Each plugin takes its thumbnail the first time you open its window. To redo it, click **Thumbnail** in the window's bar.

topics.title: Piano roll tools
topics.keywords: arpeggiator arpeggiate strum legato staccato chop glue flam claw limit flip random riff progression chords quantize groove humanize lfo rotate mute group color lasso paint slide portamento ghost score pdf mid
topics.intro: Every MIDI helper, with the result in view and in your ears before you apply it.
steps: Select notes (with none selected, the tool takes the whole clip) and open **Tools** in the piano roll's header.
A tool with settings opens a panel at the side: move the values and hear the result while it plays.
**Enter** applies and **Esc** cancels. A click on the notes applies too. Each apply is one undo step.

**Draw**, **Paint** and **Slice** change what a click on the grid does. Ctrl+Alt and drag selects with a lasso. **Length** beside them sets how long new notes are: the last note touched, the same as snap, or a fixed value.
Double-click a note to open its card: velocity, pan, release, modulation, color, slide and portamento.

**Expression**, on the bottom bar, shows or hides the lower lane, and its dropdown picks what it shows: velocity, mod X, mod Y, pan or release. **View** shows other tracks in grey and puts a waveform behind the notes. Right-click a key to name it.
In **Scale**, **MIDI keyboard to scale** lands what you play on the scale. **Arpeggiator**, in Tools, arpeggiates the keyboard and records what sounds.

topics.title: Play and record with a keyboard
topics.keywords: controller usb keyboard pedal sustain record notes
topics.intro: The keyboard plays on the selected MIDI track, with nothing to arm.
steps: Connect the keyboard. Check that its light blinks in Settings.
Select a MIDI track and play.
To record, arm it with **●** and record with {key:record}. The notes land in a clip.
notes: **Quantize while recording**, on the same page, snaps notes automatically.
Notes are written to disk as you record. If the power fails, they come back when you open the project.

topics.title: Play with the computer keyboard
topics.keywords: no keyboard virtual notes letters
topics.intro: Turns letters into piano keys.
steps: Turn it on with {key:virtualKeys}.
The **A** row is the white keys and the row above, the black ones.
**Z** and **X** change the octave; **C** and **V**, the velocity.
**Shift** is the sustain pedal.
notes: While it's on, those letters don't work as shortcuts.
With a **scale** chosen, the **Z**, **A** and **Q** rows are three octaves of the scale, 7 notes each from the root. The octave moves to **O** and **P**, and the velocity to **L** and **;**.
With **Chords** on, each key plays its note's chord.
With an instrument's window open, the keys play on its track.
The button at the end of the settings opens it in its own window. Closing that window brings it back. With little height it shows only the keys.

topics.title: Repeat a pattern
topics.keywords: loop rhythm drums link same clips fl studio instruments ghost notes
topics.intro: Linked clips: editing one changes them all.
steps: Press **Convert to pattern** at the top of the piano roll, or right-click a MIDI clip → **Convert to pattern**.

With several MIDI clips selected, right-click one: **Convert to one pattern** makes a single pattern as long as all of them together (each track, an instrument); **Convert to separate patterns**, one per clip.
Duplicate or copy the clip: the copy stays linked. Its clips carry the chain icon, and pointing at one marks them all.
Stretch a clip by its right edge to repeat the loop.
**Several instruments**: in the piano roll, **Pattern** → **Add instrument**. Each one goes on its own track, with its own notes, and a line joins the clips that play together.
**Pattern** also holds the length of the pass; in its list of instruments, a click moves to another instrument and the eye shows or hides its ghost notes.
**Make unique** takes a clip out of the pattern.
notes: A pattern's instruments move, stretch and duplicate together. Shift+edge stretches just one; Delete removes only the selected one.
The **Patterns** tab lists them. Drag them onto any MIDI track; with several instruments, each lands on its own track.
Opening a pattern clip shows a single loop. The tab also renames and deletes them.

categories.title: Analysis and separation
categories.hint: Split stems, extract MIDI and detect chords.

topics.title: Separate vocals, drums and bass
topics.keywords: stems demucs remove vocals karaoke isolate instruments backing track advanced model passes selection
topics.intro: Splits an audio clip into tracks. The original stays muted and untouched.
steps: Right-click an audio clip → **Split into stems…**.
Choose how many: 2, 4 or 6.
Choose the quality. The estimated time is shown.

In **Advanced**: the model (General, Per stem or 6 stems), which stems, how many passes, only the timeline selection instead of the whole clip, and whether the original track is muted, keeps playing or loses the clip.
Each stem lands on its own track, in a new folder.
notes: It needs the models: install them in **Settings → Components**. It's one undo step.
It uses the video card if there is a compatible one. While it runs, **Cancel separation**, in the notice, stops it.

topics.title: Turn audio into MIDI notes
topics.keywords: transcribe extract convert sheet music
topics.intro: Pulls the notes of an audio clip onto a MIDI track.
steps: Right-click the clip → **Extract MIDI**.
Choose **Chords** or **Melody**.
The notes land on a new MIDI track below. **Show notes** opens the piano roll.

topics.title: Detect the scale and chords
topics.keywords: key harmony what key is it figure out song
topics.intro: Listens to a clip and says what scale it's in.
steps: Right-click an audio clip → **Detect scale and chords**.
Check the scale, its notes and the chords.
Check **Add the chords to the timeline** to see them above the ruler.
notes: The percentages are estimates of how sure the reading is.

categories.title: Projects and files
categories.hint: Saving, recordings, disk space and sharing.

topics.title: Save the project
topics.keywords: autosave lose changes automatic saving
topics.intro: By default, each change is saved by itself after 1.5 seconds.
steps: Check the status next to the project name: **Saved**, **Saving** or **Unsaved**.
To force it, use {key:save} or the disk icon {icon:E74E}.
In **Settings → Saving and export** you can choose when it saves: on each edit, every few minutes or by hand.
notes: Recordings and exports always save, whatever the mode.

topics.title: Save as or save a copy
topics.keywords: save as copy another folder usb drive location xtp file move
topics.intro: A project can be saved in any folder. Its file is **Name.xtp**, next to its media and exports folders.
steps: In **Projects**, click the save button {icon:E792} on the row, or use {key:saveAs} with the project open.
Choose **Save as…** to keep working in the copy, or **Save a copy…** to stay in the original.
Choose the folder and the name. In an empty folder, the project goes right there; in any other, a folder with its name is created.
notes: The original is left as it is. Exports and saved versions are not copied.
To open it later, double-click the .xtp or use **Open…** in Projects. With XTreme open, it opens in that window in place of the current one.
If a double click does not open XTreme, use **Associate .xtp files with XTreme** in Settings → File association.
WildTrack projects open with **Open…** too: choose their **guitarcam.json** and it becomes a .xtp.

topics.title: Find recordings and free up space
topics.keywords: library deleted channel take recover disk full space unused recycle bin offline moved file missing linked copy
topics.intro: **Library**, in the right panel, lists everything recorded and imported: used or not.
steps: Listen to each one with its play button.
Drag it onto the timeline to use it again, or click **Use**: it goes to the selected track, at the playhead (with no track selected, to a new one).

**Delete unused** sends the project's files that aren't on the timeline to the Recycle Bin. Linked ones have their own button, **Unlink unused**: they leave the project and their files stay where they are.
notes: Removing a clip from the timeline never deletes its file.
A channel whose file is missing shows the **Offline** mark and the buttons to find it again.

topics.title: Move a project to another PC
topics.keywords: share zip package backup copy transfer
topics.intro: A package is a ZIP with everything needed.
steps: In **Projects**, click the row's package button.
Choose **To share** (what plays) or **Full backup** (also unused audio, versions and exports).
On the other side, **Open package…** brings it in as a new project.

topics.title: Edit together live
topics.keywords: collaborate live session share together internet remote distance local network vpn tailscale zerotier invite code link
topics.intro: Several people edit the same project at once, each on their own PC, and see the others' changes instantly.
steps: The host opens the project, clicks **Live session** (next to Export) picks **Create session** and where the others are: **Internet** (from anywhere) or **Local network** (same network or a VPN, direct, no server).

Over the internet, they pass on the short code (like “abc-defg-hij”) or the link; on the local network, the **code**, the **link** or the **IP** (Copy code / Copy link / Copy IP). Over the internet everything goes through XTreme's session server, encrypted end to end: the server can't read the project or the audio.
Each guest clicks **Live session → Join**, types or pastes the code and clicks **Join**: they get a copy of the project with its audio, kept in their projects.
Everyone edits everything; each one listens on their own (Play, solos and the audio interface are each one's). What's recorded reaches the others when the take ends.

Each person has a color. Their name shows on the track and clip they have selected, on what they are editing and on the track they record or play on; their playhead shows as a line in their color while they play. Their mouse is an arrow in their color with their name: over the timeline it follows their mouse, and when they grab a control (a fader, a knob, a button) in the mixer or the inspector, it points at that control on your screen, or at their track if you don't have it in view. In **History**, each step shows who made it (each person undoes only their own); in **Library**, each take shows who brought it.

A session only uses plugins everyone has. One someone lacks is greyed out in the menus and says who doesn't have it. If it was already in the project (an instrument or effect on a track, a folder or a bus), it stays off for everyone, showing «Missing on name · off», until everyone has it: the effect lets the sound through and the instrument is silent. Once it's installed, scan for plugins again and it turns on by itself.
In the session each person shows with their color, role, connection latency and what they're doing. A notice and a short sound tell you when someone joins or leaves.

Everyone needs the same XTreme version; on the local network, also the same network or a VPN such as Tailscale or ZeroTier. While it lasts, the button says **Live** and how many are in; from there, **End session** (host) or **Leave session** (guest), which keeps your copy as it is.

categories.title: Customize
categories.hint: Shortcuts, theme, window layout and language.

topics.title: See and change shortcuts
topics.keywords: keyboard keys list combinations layout cubase logic fl studio reaper fender studio pro other daw
topics.intro: The main ones, with the keys you have set:
steps: Play and stop: {key:play}. Record: {key:record}. Arm: {key:arm}.
Click: {key:click}. Tuner: {key:tuner}. Loop: {key:loop}.
Mute: {key:mute}. Solo: {key:solo}. Mixer: {key:mixer}. Fit all: {key:fit}.
Split: {key:split}. Duplicate: {key:duplicate}. Undo: {key:undo}. Save: {key:save}.
notes: **Keyboard shortcuts** has the full list, and any of them can be changed.
The search box above the Settings tabs (**Ctrl+F**) finds any option or shortcut by name: click a result to go there.
In **Key layout**, choose the keys of Cubase, Logic Pro, FL Studio, Reaper or Studio Pro. Your changes are kept in each one. What that DAW doesn't have keeps XTreme's key.

With a plugin's window in front, keys go to XTreme: transport, shortcuts and the virtual keyboard (except Alt+Tab and Alt+F4). With **Keys to plugin** on in its window's bar, every key goes to the plugin while its window is in front, and the virtual keyboard doesn't play. It applies to every plugin window.

topics.title: Change the color and layout
topics.keywords: theme accent appearance vertical panels hide full screen knobs style neumorphic faders meters waveforms font typeface numbers digital segment lcd orbitron tron legacy brightness contrast saturation warmth whole theme colors gradient custom surprise reset factory size scale zoom
topics.intro: Most of it is in the title bar.
steps: The theme picker chooses the accent color and background, and adjusts them: **Brightness**, **Contrast**, **Saturation** and **Warmth** (double-click one to reset it to 0). The same is in **Settings → Appearance → General → Theme**, which also has **Tron Legacy**, under Whole themes, that changes everything at once: background, accent, panels, knobs, faders, meters, waves and numbers; each part can be changed afterwards.
The layout button {icon:E80A} switches between **Classic** and **Vertical**.
The two panel buttons hide the sides.
{key:fullScreen} goes full screen.

In **Settings → Appearance** pick the style of the window's panels (flat, raised or raised with a gradient), of knobs, faders, meters and waveforms, how each track's color shows in the timeline (soft, solid, wave-only or title-bar clips; the header with an edge, a band, tinted, filled or no color, a tinted lane and the selection in its color), how **folders** look (frame, a block of their color or a line at the side), the **mixer strips** (cards or joined; the channel color as an edge, a band, tinted, a filled header or none) and in the inspector (rule and tint, rule only, filled or no color; a stripe along the edge, tinted sections and section icons in its color), the interface's font, the numbers' font (values, times and the clock; also a 14-segment digital one and Orbitron) the **meter colors** (**Default**, or **Custom**: pick Low, Hot and Clip, or hit **Surprise me** to draw three that go together; they apply to every meter and look, and the thresholds stay the same) and the size, in px (also with **Ctrl +** and **Ctrl −**; **Ctrl 0** goes back to 100 %), and the design of the timeline and mixer **separators** (double line, single line, band, label or groove). **Reset**, above each one, takes it back to the factory setting. The options come in groups (General, Controls, Timeline, Inspector, Mixer, Separators): click a title to open or fold it, and it stays as you left it.

topics.title: Move a panel to its own window
topics.keywords: undock dock separate window floating other monitor second monitor detach panels
topics.intro: Any panel can go to a window of its own, on another monitor for instance.
steps: Press {icon:E8A7}, at the top right of each panel. Also from **View → Panels in windows**.
What stays in the main window takes the free room. With the video out, the timeline moves up and the mixer goes under it.
Mixer, piano roll and mastering each go to a window of their own, so all three can be in sight. Each window shows only its own view: what stays in opens at the bottom of the main window.
{key:maximize} inside one of these windows maximizes it; again, and it goes back to its size.
{icon:E944} or the window's X brings it back to the main window. The window remembers its place and size, and what was out goes out again when XTreme opens.

topics.title: Change the language
topics.keywords: english spanish espanol translation
topics.intro: It applies when you restart the app. Projects don't change.
steps: Choose the language.
Close and reopen XTreme.

categories.title: If something doesn't work
categories.hint: No sound, dropouts, shifted channels, camera, plugins and FFmpeg.

topics.title: I can't hear anything
topics.keywords: no sound mute silent nothing plays
topics.intro: Check in this order.
steps: See if the master meter moves. If it does, the problem is in the output.
Check **Output** in Settings and the volume on your interface and headphones.
Check that no track has **S** on and that yours doesn't have **M** on.
If **Buffer** says **No audio** on that page, click **Refresh devices**.

topics.title: My interface doesn't show up
topics.keywords: asio driver not found not detected sound card
topics.intro: XTreme needs an ASIO driver.
steps: Install the ASIO driver from the interface's maker.
Connect it and turn it on.
Close other programs that are using it.
Click **Refresh devices**.

topics.title: Audio drops out or clicks
topics.keywords: crackling glitch pops skips stutter buffer cpu dsp
topics.intro: It's nearly always a lack of processing time.
steps: Check **DSP** in the title bar. If it's high, the processor can't keep up.
Raise the **Buffer** from **Driver panel**.
Turn off heavy instrument plugins while recording.
Try **FX** in the mixer: it bypasses all effects so you can compare.
notes: It doesn't happen in exports: they aren't rendered in real time.

topics.title: My channel lands out of time
topics.keywords: out of sync shifted late click doesnt match
topics.intro: Your interface's real latency hasn't been measured yet.
steps: Calibrate in **Settings → Sync**.
Record again: it's compensated automatically.
On an old channel, use **Audio offset**, or move it with **Alt** to free it from the grid.

topics.title: The camera doesn't show up
topics.keywords: no picture black webcam droidcam video not visible
topics.intro: Check in this order.
steps: Make sure the project is **Video + audio**.
Close other programs that use the camera.
Choose it again in Settings.
For a phone, use **IP DroidCam** with the IP and port it shows.
notes: The camera needs FFmpeg.

topics.title: FFmpeg is missing
topics.keywords: cant export video mp3 disabled error components install
topics.intro: FFmpeg is needed for the camera, video, MP3 and some formats.
steps: Open **Components**.
Install FFmpeg.
Try again.
notes: If you installed it with winget, the app finds it even when it isn't on the PATH.

topics.title: A plugin won't open or show up
topics.keywords: vst wont load crash closed error failure
topics.intro: A failing plugin doesn't bring the app down.
steps: If it closed, click **Open it again** in the notice.
If it's not listed, click **Scan for new** in Plugins.
If it's among the ones that didn't open, read the reason and click **Try again**.
notes: VST3 and VST2 plugins are supported, 64 and 32 bits. When a plugin comes in both formats, the VST2 or 32-bit one says so in the list.

topics.title: My MIDI keyboard makes no sound
topics.keywords: not detected controller no notes
topics.intro: Check in this order.
steps: Check that the device's light blinks when you play. If not, nothing is arriving.
Make sure it's on and that no other program is using it.
Select a MIDI track: the keyboard plays on the selected track.

topics.title: A clip is gray
topics.keywords: offline missing file lost
topics.intro: Its file is missing from the project's **media** folder.
steps: If you moved files out of the project folder, put them back.
Open the project again.
notes: To move a project, use a package: it carries everything.

topics.title: The project opens read-only
topics.keywords: cant edit locked another window
topics.intro: Another XTreme window has that project open, or it was saved with a newer version.
steps: Close the other window and open it again.
If it was saved with a newer version, update XTreme.

topics.title: Report a bug or suggest something
topics.keywords: comments feedback problem bug idea issue github support
topics.intro: Reports go to GitHub, where anyone can see them. You need a free account.
steps: Open **Help → Send feedback**, or click it in About.
Choose **Bug** or **Suggestion** and write a title and the description.
Check the information included and untick it if you don't want to send it.
Click **Continue on GitHub**, review the report and send it from that page.
If the text is long, it is copied to the clipboard: paste it into the description.
